_about: English for the bundled views (views/*.json), by view file and chart id; null = not translated yet (the original is shown). Format: backend/engine/wko5expr/viewi18n.py. Glossary: backend/i18n/glossary.json.

tis-per-workout.title: Aerobic / anaerobic TIS (per activity)
tis-per-workout.description:
Aerobic and anaerobic Training Impact Score (TIS) of every activity with power.
How to read: blue dot = aerobic TIS, red dot = anaerobic TIS, a whole number from 1 to 10; higher = a bigger stimulus to that energy system. Equal scores overlap; hover for the numbers.
Look for: long sessions near threshold score high aerobically; only intervals and races above threshold score high anaerobically. A high anaerobic score every day = hard sessions packed too close.
Method: WKO5's TIS: smoothed power, weighted second by second against the mFTP (aerobic) and FRC (anaerobic) of the PD model over the 90 days up to the activity. Needs power (Stryd, watch power); activities without power are not drawn.

tis-load.title: Aerobic / anaerobic long- and short-term load (TIS)
tis-load.description:
Like the PMC, but the daily stimulus split into an aerobic and an anaerobic pair of lines.
How to read: blue = aerobic, red = anaerobic; thick solid line = long-term (42 days, as CTL), thin dashed line = short-term (7 days, as ATL).
Look for: a rising long-term line = that kind of stimulus is building up: in the base phase the aerobic line rises and the anaerobic one stays low; it rises once the specific phase adds intervals. A short-term line far above its long-term line = more of that stimulus lately than usual.
Method: WKO5's Chronic / Acute TIS Load: the day's TIS summed, then the same exponential average as CTL and ATL (time constants from the settings). Only activities with power count.

long-run-km.title: Long-run distance (road runs ≥ 90 min)
long-run-km.description:
Distance of every road run of 90 minutes or more.
How to read: blue bar = one long run.
Look for: bars stepping up, then coming down in the taper.
Method: Pfitzinger, Advanced Marathoning: the long run is the key marathon session; the longest runs of the specific phase are about 32–35 km.

long-run-pace.title: Long-run pace (road runs ≥ 90 min)
long-run-pace.description:
Average moving pace of every road run of 90 minutes or more.
How to read: one dot per long run; faster is better.
Look for: the same easy long run getting faster at the same heart rate = aerobic progress; marathon-pace segments make it a bit faster in the specific phase. Read the trend, not single runs (weather, route).
Method: moving pace (stops excluded).

mp-weekly.title: Weekly marathon-pace time
mp-weekly.description:
Time per week at marathon pace.
How to read: orange bar = one week.
Look for: growing through the specific phase; near zero in the base phase is normal.
Method: marathon pace = threshold pace × 1.04–1.08 (estimate: centre × 1.06); needs a threshold pace (set or estimated). Pfitzinger's marathon-pace long runs, Canova's specific sessions.

long-run-km-specific.title: Long-run distance (road runs ≥ 90 min)
long-run-km-specific.description:
Distance of every road run of 90 minutes or more.
